issue_context.title: Insert 3 bytes of data into gbk column, result is inconsistent with MySQL
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)
```
set names gbk;
create table t3(a char(10) charset gbk);
insert into t3 values('一a');
```

```
xxx> select @@sql_mode;
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| @@sql_mode                                                                                                                                |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY,STRICT_TRANS_TABLES,NO_ZERO_IN_DATE,NO_ZERO_DATE,ERROR_FOR_DIVISION_BY_ZERO,NO_AUTO_CREATE_USER,NO_ENGINE_SUBSTITUTION |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)
```

<!-- a step by step guide for reproducing the bug. -->

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)
```
mysql> insert into t3 values('一a');
ERROR 1366 (HY000): Incorrect string value: '\x80a' for column 'a' at row 1
```

### 3. What did you see instead (Required)
```
tidb> insert into t3 values('一a');
Query OK, 1 row affected (0.00 sec)
```

### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)

<!-- Paste the output of SELECT tidb_version() -->
master
comments:
> This is the GBK incompatibility between MySQL and Golang package `simplifiedchinese`:
> 
> ```go
> // Microsoft's Code Page 936 extends GBK 1.0 to encode the euro sign U+20AC
> // as 0x80. The HTML5 specification at http://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#gbk
> // says to treat "gbk" as Code Page 936.
> case c0 == 0x80:
> 	r, size = '€', 1
> ```
> 
> `0x80` is a valid character in `simplifiedchinese`..

ok, that explains.
https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/30757/files#r774325510 Seems still have some problems with `insert` statement.

review_comments: how about add `\x80`  into the middle of the string?
in golang lib, it write `utf8.RuneError` with no error
